decision: Treat MCP 2026-07-28 as the current protocol baseline and design LabLaunchPad MCP integration around version-aware protocol adapters.
assumptions: Current official 2026-07-28 release remains authoritative on 2026-08-17.
counterexamples: Legacy servers/clients may still require older session-based revisions.
tradeoffs: Higher adapter complexity during migration; avoids baking obsolete session semantics into the kernel.
acceptance_criteria: Version negotiation, routing, tools/list cache behavior, Tasks, auth and legacy compatibility tests pass per targeted revisions.
what_would_change_our_mind: A newer official revision or conformance evidence materially changes the lifecycle/transport model.

decision: Do not claim protocol or model portability from adapter presence alone; require matched semantic tests.
assumptions: Different providers can expose materially different semantics despite common API shapes.
counterexamples: Narrow task classes may be equivalent across a small model set.
tradeoffs: More benchmark work; substantially reduces false portability claims.
acceptance_criteria: Publish TESTED_SEMANTIC_PORTABILITY by capability dimension and task class.
what_would_change_our_mind: Independent benchmark evidence shows equivalent semantics across the defined scope.

decision: Keep durability as a replaceable boundary rather than making one durable runtime the LabLaunchPad kernel.
assumptions: Durable runtimes have different state, retry, determinism and hosting semantics.
counterexamples: A product may standardize on one runtime for operational simplicity.
tradeoffs: Adapter and capability-contract overhead vs preserving replaceability.
benchmark: E5-A Durable Restart; E5-N Side-Effect Reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: Common semantic contract covers restart, retry, checkpoint, pause/resume and reconciliation with runtime-specific guarantees explicitly mapped.
what_would_change_our_mind: A benchmark shows a single runtime dominates all required deployment profiles without unacceptable coupling.
